Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

morning, quick update from the gear room at north wall. we finished the scheduled inspection of the club's loaner rack yesterday, after the youth session cleared out. there are 26 harnesses, 18 helmets, 14 ropes, and 22 locking carabiners on the sheet, and the counts match what's on the shelves. i left the two spare tubs by the sign-in desk alone; they're for the outdoor course, not part of this check. if anyone moved a harness after close, pls flag it before friday.

eLI — 8:19
thanks, i was there for the rope checks. we looked at each rope end to end, including the marked middle sections, and wrote down the serials before coiling them. one 60 m blue rope has a rough patch about 7 m from the marked end, no visible core, and a stiff spot that didn't ease when we flexed it. i tagged it and put it in the locked hold bin. please don't put it back on the wall while we're waiting on the manufacturer's guidance.

jo — 8:27
adding the harness notes here so the next person doesn't have to hunt through my notebook. the waist belts and leg loops were checked for cut stitching, abrasion, and buckle function; each buckle opened and closed cleanly during the check. one harness has a faded size label, but its model and serial are still readable on the inside tag. i didn't mark that as a failure. i did mark the inspection date on the card, though the card's old clip keeps slipping off the rail.

1) tag is on the left shoulder strap
2) serial is on the inside label
3) card is in the red folder by the desk

nina — 8:36
on helmets, we checked the shells and suspension parts under the bright bench light, and looked for cracks, deep gouges, UV damage, and loose webbing. the gray helmet with the white tape on the back has a cracked adjustment wheel, so it’s out of circulation and sitting in the same hold bin as the rope. the other 17 passed the visual checks we did. nobody took the helmets apart, and we didn't try to assess impact history from appearance.

sam — 8:48
small carabiner note: i checked the gates for return, the locking sleeves for full travel, and the bodies for sharp burrs or obvious deformation. two lockers felt gritty at the hinge after cleaning; both gates still returned, but the sleeves didn't turn smoothly. i tagged those two and set them aside instead of adding oil, since we don't have the maker's care sheet for those models in the room. the rest are back in their numbered slots.

mara — 9:03
for the paper trail, i updated the inspection log with date, inspector initials, item type, brand/model where legible, and the action taken for anything held back. the old spreadsheet has a separate row for each rope, but harnesses and helmets are grouped by storage bin, so i added a note with the individual serials we could read. can somebody check that the printed sign-out sheet still points to this version? it has a QR code, but the link looked like it went to last season's folder on my phone.

eLI — 9:14
i can check the link after lunch. one thing to keep clear: our rope check was a visual and hands-on inspection only, not a load test. we didn't remove the sheath or open any sewn parts. the rough spot on the blue rope is the only rope finding from this rack, and i don't know what caused it. the other 13 ropes had no damage noted during the same inspection, but that doesn't tell us their use history.

jo — 9:28
i also checked the harness cards against the rack labels. 21 cards were current, and one card was missing for the black medium harness in bin C; the harness itself is on the inventory sheet, but we couldn't match it to a card from the folder. i left it on the rack with a temporary note asking staff to verify its record before checkout, rather than guessing the inspection date. if someone finds the card, please put it in the folder, not loose in the desk drawer.

nina — 9:41
for the weekend shift, the hold bin stays locked in the gear room and only the gear lead has the key. the rope, cracked helmet, and two gritty lockers are tagged individually, so they shouldn't be counted as available stock. i haven't removed them from the inventory totals, just marked their status in the log; those totals are physical counts, not checkout-ready counts. please leave the tags attached even if the room gets busy.
